A heavy shot of economic news rolls out before the market opens: import/export prices, weekly jobless claims and regional manufacturing gauges from the New York and Philadelphia Federal Reserve banks. After the open, the builders confidence index from the National Association of Homebuilders is due out at 10 a.m. ET. 
Markets in Asia generally posted mild gains Thursday: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index rose 0.3%. Tokyo's Nikkei 225 added 0.1%. Europe's markets were higher near midday with Frankfurt's DAX leading the main benchmarks, up 0.3%. Exxon Leads Dow; Alexion, Semtech, Dollar General Surge 
Early trade on the Dow was tight, with Exxon-Mobil pushing ahead 0.9% as the ups and downs held to moves of less than 1%. 
Apple ( AAPL ) dipped 0.1%, and the four FANG stock tech leaders were mixed. Facebook ( FB ) notched the largest mover in either direction, down 0.4%. Facebook shares are up 10% from an early February low, and in the sixth week of a flat-base pattern . 
Alexion Pharmaceuticals sailed 8% higher, after announcing positive results in a phase 3 trial of its rare blood disorder treatment ALXN1210. The stock's long consolidation has produced an odd and flawed base pattern, with potential buy points at 129.35 and 149.44. Shares ended Wednesday 5% below the 129.35 entry. 
Earnings drove some of the largest premarket moves, with Papa Murphys Holdings ( FRSH ) rocketing 16% following a solid fourth-quarter report late Wednesday. The chain offering fresh, cook-at-home pizzas trades below 10. 
Dollar General popped 8% despite a relatively weak fourth-quarter performance, although Q4 same-store-sales topped analyst expectations and the company provided above-expectation Q1 guidance, hoisted its dividend 12%, raised its launched a $1 billion share buyback. The stock is down 16% from a late-January high, in the seventh week of a consolidation. 
Chipmaker Semtech bolted 12% higher as fourth-quarter results squeaked past analysts' targets. The stock closed Wednesday's session 13% below a 39.50 buy point in a double-bottom base . 
Additive print technology leader 3D Systems ( DDD ) whipped up a 95 premarket gain. The Rock Hill, South Carolina company reported EPS of 5 cents, vs. consensus views for 3 cents. Revenue rose 7%, well above expectations and the company biggest advance since Q2 2015. 3D shares were testing resistance at their 40-week moving average, up 53% from a November low and climbing the right side of a deep, 10-month consolidation. 
Action among China-based stocks was mixed, as BitAuto Holdings ( BITA ) climbed 4% after turning in a positive fourth-quarter report. Online travel service Ctrip.com International tumbled 6%, its fourth-quarter results and first quarter guidance, reported late Wednesday, fell short of consensus targets.
